destination.name: Newcastle
destination.tagline: A port city with surf beaches, ocean baths and a harbour fort, north of Sydney.
destination.description: Newcastle sits at the mouth of the Hunter River about 150 km north of Sydney, and is NSW's second population centre, with 349,000 people in the City of Newcastle (2021). It is Australia's oldest seaport and the world's largest coal-exporting port, yet its beaches, ocean baths and headland fort are a short walk from the centre. The destination reaches south to Lake Macquarie's beaches and west to Blackbutt Reserve and Mount Sugarloaf. Newcastle Museum fills three old railway workshops, and Newcastle Art Gallery's ground-floor collection is free.
whyVisit: Swim in Newcastle's historic ocean baths
Walk the pier out to Nobbys Head
Tour the tunnels at Fort Scratchley

goodToKnow.title: Baths close one day a week
goodToKnow.detail: Newcastle Ocean Baths close on Wednesdays and Merewether Ocean Baths on Thursdays for cleaning, with change rooms opening from 5:30 am on other days.

goodToKnow.title: Nobbys Head opening
goodToKnow.detail: The headland grounds at Nobbys Head are open weekends and public holidays, 8 am to 4 pm, so weekday visitors can only reach the pier.

goodToKnow.title: Train and light rail
goodToKnow.detail: Trains from Sydney take 2 to 3 hours to Newcastle Interchange, where light rail runs to the city centre and beach; the Opal card works on the train.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: summers are warm and humid and suit the surf beaches and ocean baths, though hot north-westerlies can occasionally push temperatures past 40C.
